                  Definition 8. Rectangle [00GL]

                    The authors in arXiv:math/0503436v2 define a square on a finite set to be a pair of equivalence relations such that every equivalence class of intersect every equivalance class of in exactly one element.

                    This structure was first introduced in arXiv:math/0210057v2 under the term cartesian decomposition.

                            13. General Decompositions vs non-degenerate decompositions [00GV]

                              Pro general

                              • its the simpler definition
                              • mirros what happens with natural numbers: any natural number divides
                              • dirichlet convolution as pointwise cartesian product works even if F and G do not vanish on empty set

                              Pro non-degenerate

                              • its equivalent to what people use in the literature
                              • its a tame species
                              • dirichlet product of tame species is always tame, no matter what happens on empty set

                              To be decided

                              • What works better with dirichlet powers and the dirichlet exponential?
